key_insight: Bulky ligand substituents suppress intermolecular magnetic interactions in a five-Cu(II) metallacrown, revealing competing antiferromagnetic couplings and an intrinsic S = 1/2 ground state.
engineering_relevance: Steric ligand design offers a route to magnetically isolate molecular spin clusters for studying exchange interactions and anisotropy.
method: Modify salicylhydroxamate ligands with bulky substituents.
Probe magnetism using static magnetization and X-band/high-field EPR.
Compare exchange couplings and g-factors with broken-symmetry DFT.
evidence_signal: Magnetization yields J₁ = −8.1(2) THz and J₂ = −4.40(12) THz, corroborated by DFT, while EPR resolves g = (2.028, 2.056, 2.222) and supports a thermally accessible quartet excitation.
watch_item: The S = 1/2 ground-state description applies at low temperatures; thermal population across the 4.8(4) THz doublet–quartet gap must be considered.
paper_title: Magnetism in a homometallic square-planar Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$$_4$Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$ metallacrown
